items.title: Norway hands out $430m for floating offshore wind projects
points: Norway’s state-backed Enova has awarded NOK3.94bn ($430m) in funding to two floating offshore wind projects to install four next-generation turbines off Karmøy.
Fortius Offshore Wind and Fram Wind Solutions have been selected to receive support for projects at the METCentre offshore wind demonstration facility in Rogaland.
The awards follow a competitive funding process that attracted five applications.
Fortius, owned by Deep Wind Offshore, has been allocated NOK2bn, while Fram Wind Solutions, backed by BW Offshore and Grieg Kapital, will receive NOK1.94bn.
Each project will comprise two floating turbines rated at 18.5MW, giving the developments a combined capacity of 74MW.
The installations are expected to generate approximately 300GWh of electricity annually, equivalent to the consumption of around 15,000 households.
Both developers plan to install their turbines within the next five years, with funding to be paid out subject to the projects being realised.
The projects will test floating foundations capable of supporting large turbines, mooring systems and new approaches to offshore construction, installation and operation.

The private sector HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) fell to 54.7 in October 2026 as compared to 55.1 in September.
A reading over 50 denotes expansion, while one below 50 shows contraction in activity.

points: Iran has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington meets its conditions, offering a breakthrough in talks to end the war as both sides warn that renewed fighting could spread regionally.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Qatari mediators had helped shorten Tehran’s seven-day reopening proposal.

items.title: Vale freight, fuel hedges cushion impact of rising shipping costs
points: Brazilian miner Vale SA’s freight and fuel hedging strategies have protected the company from the worst impacts of higher shipping costs facing iron ore producers, CEO Gustavo Pimenta said.
About 75% of Vale’s shipping needs are covered by long-term contracts at fixed prices over the next few years, while the remaining needs will be managed through shorter-term contracts.
Vale’s realized freight costs increased by $4.70/metric ton since the first quarter, much less than the spot cost from Brazil to China, according to Pimenta.
Over the same period, spot freight rates for the Brazil-China route increased by $12/mt, compared with $4.90/mt for the route from Australia to China, Pimenta said.
The iron ore dry-bulk freight for Tubarão, Brazil, to Qingdao, North China, on a 170,000 Capesize basis assessed by Platts, part of S&P Global, peaked at $43.35/wet metric ton on Sept.

items.title: The cost of almost: what trade at its full potential really means
points: At any given moment, thousands of vessels are at sea.
Each voyage is shaped by a series of decisions: speed, route, fuel, vessel performance, timing and execution.
There is rarely one obviously right choice.
A slower vessel may burn less fuel but arrive too late to capture the value of the cargo.
A faster voyage may cost more in bunkers but create a better commercial outcome.
The same operational decisions shape cost, voyage economics, resilience and emissions.
Trade operating at its full potential therefore means balancing them well: commercially precise, operationally resilient and environmentally responsible as the natural outcome of better operations.
That is what full potential looks like: better use of the information, assets and choices now available – and less avoidable waste in how the system operates.

items.title: Kumiai Navigation takes delivery of LPG dual-fuel gas carrier
points: Singapore shipowner Kumiai Navigation’s new gas carrier from Kawasaki Heavy Industries (KHI) could later be converted to run on ammonia.
The 86,700-cbm gas carrier Aurora Borealis has separate cargo tanks so it can carry liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and ammonia at the same time.
It is the 14th ship in KHI’s series of LPG dual-fuel carriers for LPG and ammonia, and the 21st LPG-capable vessel the shipbuilder has completed.

KHI has delivered three other LPG-capable ships in the series this year: In January, KHI delivered Lucent Pathfinder, which Japanese shipping company NYK Line named earlier that month for charter to energy firm BGN.
In April, Kumiai Navigation received Aurora Guardian, sister ship to Aurora Borealis.
In August, Lyla Pathfinder became NYK Line’s eighth LPG dual-fuel carrier and joined BGN on charter.
There are 183 LPG dual-fuel vessels in operation globally, with another 184 on order through 2030, according to DNV data.
Source: By Nachiket Tekawade, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news/

points: China and Russia are tightening their grip on Arctic shipping routes, turning the rapidly warming region into a new geopolitical battleground with Europe.
Moscow and Beijing last week have agreed to expand freight traffic along Arctic shipping corridors, increase services between their ports and deepen cooperation on building polar vessels.
The agreement came after the EU unveiled a new Arctic strategy aimed at countering growing Russian and Chinese influence in the region.

Although the competing moves underscore how the once-remote region is turning into a strategic prize, analysts said that Europe’s ability to challenge the emerging China-Russia partnership remains limited, given Moscow’s control over the main shipping…

items.title: 22 deaths worldwide involving EU ships in 2025
points: In 2025, there were 22 fatalities in maritime accidents worldwide involving EU-registered ships, up by 7 from 2024.
There were also 3 fatalities in accidents within the EU territorial seas involving ships registered outside the EU.
Between 2021 and 2025, on average, 27 people died worldwide each year in maritime accidents involving EU-registered ships.
Among the 22 fatalities, 10 happened in the Atlantic Ocean, 2 each in the Mediterranean Sea and in the North Sea and 1 happened in the Baltic Sea.
Additionally, 5 were registered in the rest of the world and 2 in unknown locations.
Most of those deaths occurred in cargo ships (8) and in fishing vessels (8).
Passenger ships, recreational crafts and service ships registered 2 deaths each.
In the ‘other persons’ category, which covers service personnel, dock workers, pilots, inspectors, etc., 3 people lost their lives.

In addition to the six vessels built by Samsung Heavy Industries, CMES secured long-term transportation contracts for four larger 271,000-cubic-meter QC MAX carriers, which are being built by China’s Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding.
LNG carriers are among the most technologically demanding commercial vessels, as they transport natural gas at temperatures of around minus 162 C.
The LEKHRAIB features a GTT Mark III Flex membrane containment system, with a designed daily boil-off rate of no more than 0.085 percent, as well as dual-fuel engines.

items.title: South Korea’s Top Shipbuilders Post Strong Q3 Profits Amid Challenges
points: Amid adverse factors such as exchange rate declines, reduced working days, and labor-management conflicts, South Korea’s three major shipbuilders achieved relatively robust performance in the third quarter of this year.
Samsung Heavy Industries announced on the 29th that its operating profit for the quarter increased by 42% compared to the same period last year.
Combined, the operating profits of the three shipbuilders—HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering and Hanwha Ocean—totaled 2.2713 trillion Korean won.

Samsung Heavy Industries reported third-quarter revenue of 3.1504 trillion Korean won and operating profit of 338.4 billion Korean won, marking year-on-year increases of 19.6% and 42.1%, respectively.
Although revenue decreased by 2.5% from the previous quarter due to reduced working days caused by summer vacations and the Chuseok holiday, operating profit rose by 4.1%.

items.title: Copper Finds Support as Tech Rout Eases
points: Copper futures climbed toward $6.50 per pound on Monday, snapping a two-day decline as the selloff in technology stocks driven by AI concerns lost momentum, lifting sentiment toward the metal.

Copper remains a key material in the global AI expansion due to its widespread use in data centers, power grids, and electrical infrastructure, making prices particularly sensitive to shifts in technology sector sentiment.

The agreement follows their selection as preferred negotiating partners in 2024.
They aim to finalise the contract value and other commercial terms before the end of 2026.

Under the proposed turnkey arrangement, LS Cable & System will manufacture the subsea cables, while LS Marine Solution will undertake offshore installation using its upgraded GL2030 cable-laying vessel.
The vessel recently completed a major upgrade that increased its cable-loading capacity from 4,000 tonnes to 7,000 tonnes.
The improvements allow it to lay cable sections exceeding 100 km continuously, reducing offshore voyages and improving installation efficiency.

items.title: China Completes Sea Trials Of An AI-Powered Crewed Submersible At 7,000 Meters That Could Help Future Nuclear Submarines
points: China recently tested an upgraded AI system onboard the Jiaolong Submersible in the Pacific Ocean, specifically the Philippine Basin.
During the trials, the crewed sub reached depths of about 23,000 feet or 7056 metres.
The tech could enhance decision making capabilities and emergency response onboard nuclear submarines, since they cannot depend on continuous satellite communication underwater.
The latter helps pilots identify issues with the onboard equipment and respond to them during dives.
According to sources, the AI system was trained using over 800,000 images which prevents it from misidentifying any object underwater.
The system can even rebuild the submarine’s course in 3-D, analyse the geological features on the course or provide any other relevant data when asked.
For example, in such a case, the system could be fed acoustic data gathered by the sonar systems of submarines, which could then help to correctly identify underwater threats.

items.title: Ather Bets On 80 Km Electric Scooters While Ola Chases 300 Km: Who Is Right?
points: Would you buy an electric scooter with 80 km of range when another manufacturer is promising 300 km?
Ather says its average customer rides just 27–28 km a day.
On that basis, a scooter capable of around 80 km in everyday use could cover roughly three days of commuting.
Ather lists a 100 km IDC version with an expected 80 km TrueRange and a 2.1 kWh battery.
Higher variants are rated at 125 km and 161 km under IDC testing, with estimated TrueRange figures of 100 km and 130 km.
Ola Electric has been promoting scooters with substantially higher claimed ranges, including a model unveiled in August with a figure of around 300 km.
Equally, a claimed 300 km under a test cycle should not be compared directly with Ather's expected 80 km real-world figure.
An 80 km usable range could work comfortably for the first, but leave the second with little reserve after accounting for hills, passengers, tyre pressure and battery ageing.

items.title: New plea in Transgender Act case before SC invites censure from trans, feminist groups
points: “Eligibility and access to all protection/ entitlements available specifically to women shall be determined by biological sex alone.” WDI India filed the petition on October 10, but it was tagged along with other challenges by a three-judge bench led by…

While Section 7 pertains to the procedure to apply for male or female gender certification upon gender affirmative surgery, Section 18 (d) punishes acts of physical, sexual, emotional, verbal and economic abuse against transgender persons for a period of…

items.title: SC to hear SP leader Azam Khan’s plea against arrest in money laundering case
points: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to hear this week Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan’s plea, challenging his arrest by Enforcement Directorate (ED) after he got bail in a dual PAN card case.
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant agreed to list the plea as he heard its urgent mention, expressing reservation over approaching the top court instead of first moving the high court.
We can relegate the matter to the high court and request the chief justice to hear it without any delay,” said CJI Kant.
Advocate Nizam Pasha, who appeared for Khan, told the court that this is a classic case of “evergreening” of arrest.
He added that an ED team arrived and arrested Khan minutes after he stepped out after getting bail on October 29.
He has been named an accused in 87 cases, and this is the 88th case.

items.title: Sonos Play Review: A Portable Speaker With a Surround Trick

On its own, it’s a solid portable speaker: IP67-rated, with a replaceable battery and reliable sound.
I spent three weeks with two Sonos Play units, running them on the new Sonos 27 software.
The Sonos Play costs Rs 35,999 for a single unit in India, available in black and white finishes through Sonos’s website and authorised retailers.

items.title: No operational fatality in 12 months for CRPF, first time in 47 years
points: The paramilitary Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has not suffered a single operational fatality anywhere in the country over a year for the first time in 47 years.

In 2024, 12 deaths were reported from Chhattisgarh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Manipur.
No fatalities since October 30, 2025, have coincided with the government’s announcement in Parliament about meeting the March 31 deadline for ending LWE.
CRPF chief GP Singh called a fatality-free year for the first time since the period ending January 1979 a significant milestone.
In 2025, the eight CRPF personnel were killed in action in LWE areas of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Odisha.

items.title: Sebi backs removal of LTCG for foreign investors: Report

Foreign investors have sold a record $31 billion in Indian stocks this year and overseas investments by retail investors have surged as returns have stagnated.

Investors currently pay long-term capital gains tax of 12.5% for securities held for more than a year and short-term capital gains tax of 20%, in addition to securities transaction taxes on trades and withholding taxes on dividends.
Brokerage firm IIFL estimates scrapping capital gains tax could lift foreign investors' returns by 2.3 percentage points.

points: (Bloomberg) -- Japan’s spot power prices surged at the weekend, with elevated fuel costs driving rates in major electricity-consuming regions Tokyo and Chubu to multi-year highs.

The next-day spot power price for the Tokyo and Chubu areas, climbed 1.1% and 7.2% on a weekly basis to ¥36.11 ($0.2)/kWh and ¥36.29/kWh respectively on Sunday, the highest since September 2022, according to data from Japan Electric Power Exchange.
Meanwhile, the nationwide average price was down 8.7% to ¥30.09/kWh on the same day.
Spot liquefied natural gas prices extended gains to about $34 per million British thermal units on Friday, according to traders, more than triple pre-war levels.
Average household electricity bills in the Tokyo area are projected to reach a record ¥9,738 in November, driven by rising fuel costs stemming from the conflict in the Middle East.

items.title: Oaktree’s Howard Marks Says AI Stumbles Boosted Skepticism
points: (Bloomberg) -- Recent artificial intelligence related market stumbles have somewhat burst the bubble of infallibility around the sector, Howard Marks, co-chair of Oaktree Capital Management LP, said in an interview with Bloomberg TV.

“I think that now people are saying, hold on, wait a minute, let’s be a little more thoughtful, let’s be a little more skeptical,” Marks, who wrote in a note last year that he was on bubble watch, said.
Recent results from Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. have fueled concerns that AI is eroding the businesses financing those investments.
Marks gained attention in January 2000 for his memo “bubble.com,” in which he warned of dot-com mania ahead of the bust.
“A trillion is $1 a second for 31,000 years,” he said.

“Nobody can think about 31,000 years or what it means.” The question investors should be asking, Marks said, is whether there can be enough business and profit to produce an attractive return on these investments.

items.title: Citi Cuts Lithium Forecasts on Worsening Battery Demand Outlook
points: (Bloomberg) -- Citigroup Inc. cut its price targets for lithium for the next two years, citing concerns over a slowdown in battery demand growth, rising trade uncertainty and broader macroeconomic headwinds.

Fears of demand deterioration for the metal next year have triggered a “lithium reset,” it said in a note by analysts including Shreyas Madabushi, warning that prices will remain depressed in the near term.

“With supply expected to improve in 2027 and uncertainty around next year’s demand elevated, consumers are likely to defer purchases and maintain lean inventories,” the bank said in the note released Friday.

“Sentiment and positioning are likely to remain the dominant drivers in the near term, keeping risks skewed to the downside.” Citi cut its three-month lithium carbonate and hydroxide price targets to $12,000 a ton from $20,000 and $17,000, respectively,…

Concrete Roads Are Bad For You And Your Car: 5 Things Nobody Tells You
points: Highway and expressway expansion works are happening in different parts of the country.

While the authorities are building roads on one side, we also come across reports and videos questioning the quality of these new roads.

Over the years, there has been an increase in the number of roads with white toppings or concrete surfaces, and anyone who has driven on such roads would agree that they are not always comfortable to drive on.
It is a type of road construction method in which a layer of Portland cement concrete (PCC) is placed directly on top of an existing damaged or worn-out bituminous (asphalt) road.
This thick layer of concrete improves the lifespan of the road to up to 50 years and eliminates the need for re-tarring every 3 to 4 years.
So, if you drive on concrete roads regularly, the life of your vehicle's tyres could decrease by anywhere between 20 and 30 percent.

items.title: Shipping Strikes In Hormuz Leave Both Sides With Economic Pain
points: U.S. Central Command/Handout via REUTERS Oct 31, 2026 (Bloomberg) –As US President Donald Trump threatens renewed attacks against Iran, Tehran’s intermittent strikes on commercial vessels have left the two sides locked in a painful economic standoff.

For Iran, the US blockade of its oil exports has snuffed out a key part of its military funding and severely hobbled the $300 billion economy, with only a tiny fraction of the prewar 2 million barrels per day are leaving the country via land routes.

And for the US, the rising cost of shipping oil through the Strait of Hormuz — even though US Central Command says almost all Iranian attacks there fail or are intercepted — has kept fuel prices high, stirring a political backlash at home with the midterm…
Iran doesn’t even need a high tempo of attacks to keep oil prices elevated; although shipments through the strait are at about 80% of prewar levels, the associated risk has inflated insurance costs.

China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island’s east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols.

points: A drone view shows the Russian-flagged tanker Bratsk, which is under U.S. sanctions for links to the Russian state-owned shipping company Sovcomflot, near the Baniyas oil terminal, in Baniyas, Syria, April 8, 2026.

REUTERS/Khalil Ashawi Oct 31, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Russia’s government has extended a general ban on diesel exports by producers until the end of January while still allowing some volumes to flow to the global market.

On Friday, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said that alongside the extension of the general export ban, the government is preparing exemptions for certain suppliers to ship diesel to global markets.
Russia relaxed the terms of its export ban this month after US President Donald Trump said he was working with President Vladimir Putin to release Russian diesel back onto global markets.

points: Iran has redirected its naval strategy amidst the threat of fresh US and Israeli strikes by broadening its attack areas in the Gulf waters.
In a latest incident, Iran used a speedboat to target a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz by attaching two limpet mines to its hull.
This is the first time that explosive devices have been used by the Islamic Republic since 2019.
The incident unfolded on Thursday night when the Dubai-owned vessel Louise 1 was sailing across the dangerous waterway.
In 2019, at least four ships, one of them being Japanese and another Norwegian, were targeted using the Limpet Mines in the Gulf of Oman.
Even during those times, tensions between Iran and the West were high after Trump decided to reimpose sanctions against Tehran’s nuclear programme and withdraw from the nuclear agreement.

The GJ-21 was first displayed at a parade in Beijing in 2025 celebrating the end of WWII.
The drone reportedly has sufficient combat radius and a small airframe compared to J-35 and J-20 stealth fighter planes.

AEB To Become Mandatory In All Cars From October 2032? MoRTH Proposes New Rules
points: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has proposed making Advanced Emergency Braking Systems (AEBS) mandatory in all passenger cars in India from October 1, 2032.
Under the draft proposal, the requirement will first apply to new car models from October 1, 2030, before being extended to all existing models two years later.
The proposal is part of a draft amendment to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, and aims to improve road safety by reducing the risk and severity of collisions.
Under the proposed Indian regulations, the system will have to comply with Automotive Industry Standard AIS-185.
From October 1, 2030, the system will become mandatory for all new M1-category car models manufactured from that date.
The requirement will then extend to all M1-category car models from October 1, 2032, including those already in production.
From October 1, 2027, vehicles equipped with these systems will have to comply with the relevant Indian automotive standards.

items.title: How Hyderabad’s Rapid Urban Growth Is Reshaping Personal Mobility
points: Hyderabad does not expand slowly; it leaps.
The Nehru Outer Ring Road (ORR) made long cross-city commutes tolerable, while the Metro made short core-city trips optional.
Between these two infrastructural forces, personal mobility in Hyderabad has quietly reorganised itself, creating a unique used-car market dynamic.
The ORR Rewrote the Rules of Car Choice Before the ORR matured, commuting from Miyapur to Madhapur meant grinding through congested inner-city signals.
Today, a significant portion of daily transit happens at steady cruising speeds of 70 to 80 kmph on the expressway.
Why New Neighbourhoods Foster Second-Car Households Watch what happens when a family relocates from a central hub like Himayatnagar to a sprawling gated community near Tellapur.
This structural reality has fueled steady, localised demand for compact, affordable used cars in the sub-six-lakh bracket.
The Shortening Replacement Cycle Vehicle owners in the IT corridor tend to upgrade faster than those in older parts of the city.

The decision means state-run oil marketing companies (OMCs) will not invite bids for ethanol produced using these sugar-based feedstocks during the upcoming supply year, which begins in November 2026.
